instructions: Answer as the intent provider for a company you run. Each item has two reasonable options; neither is wrong. Go with your first instinct, and say whether you lean slightly or clearly.

items.stem: A big order would keep the whole crew busy this month and push the new product back a quarter.

b.text: Stay on the new product

items.stem: The company had a good year and has spare cash.

a.text: Reinvest it in equipment that pays off over three years

b.text: Pay it out to the owners now

items.stem: Training everyone on a better system would mean two slow weeks.

a.text: Skip it and keep this month's pace

b.text: Do it; the company will be faster a year from now

items.stem: You want more sales.

a.text: Run a discount promotion that lifts sales this month

b.text: Build a customer email list that grows sales slowly over years

items.stem: The shop roof leaks.

a.text: Replace it for $6,000 now to avoid bigger costs later

b.text: Patch it for $800 and deal with it later

items.stem: There's a chance to launch a new product line.

a.text: 30% chance it doubles revenue, 70% chance it loses $20,000

b.text: Improve the current line for a reliable 5% gain

items.stem: The company is ready to grow.

a.text: Grow in the town you already know

b.text: Open where nobody sells what you sell, but demand is unproven

items.stem: This quarter's marketing budget.

a.text: Put 10% into a new channel nobody has tested

b.text: Keep it all on channels that already work

items.stem: One large customer wants a contract that would be half your revenue.

b.text: Keep customers small and spread out

items.stem: How much cash should the company keep on hand?

a.text: Six months of expenses, even if it sits idle

b.text: Two months, and put the rest to work

items.stem: A popular product sells well, but you think it's mediocre.

b.text: Stop selling it and lose the sales

items.stem: A supplier offers to make a cheaper line you could sell under your name.

a.text: Keep your name only on what you make yourself

b.text: Take the deal and the extra sales

items.stem: You have $2,000 to spend.

a.text: Ads that bring in measurable sales

b.text: Sponsor a local event that gets your name out but brings no direct sales

items.stem: A well-known brand with a mixed public image offers a big distribution deal.

b.text: Pass

items.stem: There's a shortage, and customers would pay more for what you sell.

b.text: Raise prices to match demand

items.stem: A customer wants the premium package, but the basic one would do everything they need.

a.text: Tell them the basic one will do

b.text: Sell them the premium package

items.stem: A supplier cuts its prices.

b.text: Pass the savings on to customers

items.stem: How should service contracts renew?

b.text: Only when the customer chooses to renew

items.stem: An order arrived late because the shipping company slipped.

a.text: Refund the shipping out of your own pocket

b.text: Apologize and point to the shipping company

items.stem: Choose a return policy.

b.text: 30 days, no questions asked

items.stem: A routine supplier bill arrives 5% higher than last month.

a.text: Pay it and note the change

b.text: Ask me before paying

items.stem: A customer asks for a small discount to close a sale.

b.text: Use your judgment up to 10%

items.stem: A cheaper shipping company with good reviews turns up.

b.text: Propose it and wait for my answer

items.stem: A social media post is drafted and ready.

b.text: Post it

items.stem: Two jobs are booked for the same morning.

a.text: Move the smaller one and let both customers know

b.text: Ask me which one moves

items.stem: Your supplier of ten years is 8% more expensive than a new one.

b.text: Switch to the new one

items.stem: A long-time customer has an old discount that makes them barely profitable.

b.text: Keep serving them as before

items.stem: Your local bookkeeper costs more than an online service.

b.text: Keep the local bookkeeper

items.stem: A partner business sends you customers but takes a lot of your time.

b.text: Scale it back

items.stem: Your biggest customer wants a quarterly update.

a.text: Email the report and save the half day

b.text: Meet them in person

items.stem: To grow sales:

a.text: Build a customer base slowly over years

b.text: Run a promotion that pays off this month

items.stem: Cash on hand:

a.text: Keep a thin cushion and invest the rest

b.text: Keep a large reserve, even if it sits idle

items.stem: Demand spikes and supply is short.

b.text: Hold your usual prices

items.stem: Your costs fall.

b.text: Keep the difference

items.stem: A regular bill comes in a little higher than usual.

b.text: Pay it and tell me

items.stem: A new supplier undercuts your long-time one by 8%.

b.text: Stay

redLines.prompt: List anything the company must never do, at any price, beyond what the law already forbids. One per line. Leave it empty if there are none.
examples: Never sell to a customer I know will misuse the product
Never lay someone off by text or email
